messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Fixing parameters in the newest unmarked version
parts:
In the meantime if the model is the simple occupancy model (no covariates, constant probability of presence and constant detection probability, and same number of visits at all sites) and the known parameter is the detection probability, then the maximum likelihood estimate of the probability of presence is

    psi-hat = min(1,(n-n0)/(n(1-(1-p)^v))

with an estimate of the asymptotic variance of

    var(psi-hat) = (n-n0)n0/(n^3(1-(1-p)^v)^2)

when 0 < psi-hat < 1 and where n is the number of sites, v is the number of visits per site, n0 is the number of sites with no detections, and p is the known detection probability.

The potential issue, of course, is "Is the detection probability really known?"  If it's "kinda" known, then maybe a Bayesian approach with a tight prior on p would be appropriate.

(Attached is a PDF document that is typeset a bit better than the above.)

Jim

messages.subject: Re: Fixing parameters in the newest unmarked version
parts:
Dear group members, 

I'm fitting dynamic occupancy wit the colext() function. 
My purpose is to model colonization and extinction probability of bird colonies located in different classes of habitat. 

Since the location of the colonies is known and the survey was realized (once per year) in all the sites, 
I want to fix the detection probability to 1, as other authors did on analogous study systems.

It is possible to do this in the colext()?

A possible trick that I imagined is to generate dummy repetition of the census within each year so that the estimated p should result 1. Would be this acceptable?

Thanks for any suggestion, 

miche
